title: A streamed response with no declared length cannot be cut off, so a body that ends early reaches the client as if it were complete.
text: `rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream` says a `Workbook::createForDownload` that is never finished is cut off, so the browser reports a failed download and not a broken file. The same holds for any streamed body: a throw, a limit FATAL or a cancel mid-stream must not look like a finished response. `nvs_runtime::stream::Emit` has one ending, `finish`, and its `Drop` calls it (`crates/nvs-runtime/src/stream.rs:260`, `:279`), so an isolate that ends for any reason ends its body cleanly (`crates/nvs-host/src/isolate.rs:1344`): `Drain::next_chunk` returns `Drained::Ended`, and the streaming body returns `Poll::Ready(None)`, the end of a complete chunked body (`crates/nvs-server/src/serve.rs:466-474`). Only a body with a declared length that ends short is aborted there, as `BodyCut::StreamEndedEarly`. The body `streamed` builds (`:2587`) already has the other ending for the drain period: it returns an error frame (`DrainPeriodEnded`) when the cut is reached, which aborts the response. Closing it means a second ending on `Emit`, an abort that `Drain` reports and this body turns into that same error frame, taken whenever the program ends with the stream unfinished.
